name: 9h nine hours Nagoya station
detail: It was my first time using Nine Hours Nagoya Station. I was very satisfied to stay for about 2,000 yen on a Sunday via Agoda. After arriving at Nagoya Station, I crossed the signal near KITTE while looking at the map, but I thought it would be closer to cross at the Dai Nagoya Building. The guest room was clean as shown in the pictures, and I surprisingly slept very well. The elevator is separate for men and women and uses a QR code for access, which is reassuring. However, since there is only one elevator, there may be a wait at times. The guest room pods and luggage lockers being on different floors allowed me to sleep peacefully. Occasionally, I encountered people rustling through their bags in the guest room, but I wish they would be more considerate. The bath towels and face towels were thick and clean, and I was glad there was also a foot mat. The lounge wear was comfortable, and the disposable slippers were a nice touch. The shower room was minimal but had shelves, which were good. The lounge on the top floor was also comfortable, making me forget that this is a capsule hotel. At Nakasu Kawabata, I was able to have my luggage stored after checkout, but it was unfortunately not possible in Nagoya.

name: HOTEL LiVEMAX NAGOYA SHINKANSENGUCHI
detail: This time, I stayed overnight to attend a live performance at Vantelin Dome. Although it was just one night, I had a lot of luggage due to support goods, and I wanted to store my bags after arriving if possible. However, when I checked with ChatGPT, I was told, This hotel doesn't seem to offer luggage storage. Considering that this information might be outdated, I asked through Agoda the day before if it was possible to store my luggage, and despite the late hour, I received a response saying, We can store your luggage from early morning on the day of check-in. By being able to store my luggage here in the morning, my subsequent movements and activities became much easier. Thank you very much. (I was also grateful that they handled the check-in process and brought my luggage to the room.) The twin non-smoking room, while not very spacious, had a separate bath and toilet and was clean. Although I didn't use it this time, having a microwave in the room is a nice feature, isn't it? The checkout process was smooth as well, just putting the card in the box, making for a very comfortable stay. At around *** yen for one person, it offers great cost performance! In the surrounding area, there's a Seven-Eleven and a Daily Store nearby, but it's relatively quiet, which is nice. There is a delicious eel Japanese restaurant called Shirakawa nearby. KANNON Coffee, located in the building right in front, is also recommended for breakfast.

name: Vessel Inn Sakae Station
detail: It's clean, soundproof, and the room is fine. The front desk staff are friendly. The free drinks at the second-floor lounge are great. Plus, they serve alcoholic beverages until 7 PM. When I went, there was record-breaking heavy rain, so I spent time enjoying a drink in the lounge. There's a Seven Eleven on the first floor, so you can buy food and eat it in the lounge. They say there's a bustling area and nightlife behind the building, but it wasn't noisy at all. I'm very satisfied with the bed and pillows.

name: Nagoya Tokyu Hotel
detail: I have occasionally used this place since long ago. The room was clean and well-maintained, and when I requested a quiet room, they placed me in a room far from the elevator, allowing me to relax in the morning! The parking lot is narrow, which is a bit of a challenge, but other than that, I am satisfied with the staff's service and everything else.

name: Natural Hot Spring Hotel LiVEMAX PREMIUM Nagoya Marunouchi
detail: It was very convenient to have an English-speaking staff member. I appreciated that pajamas were provided, so I didn’t have to pack my own. The hot water worked well and had great pressure. There was also a microwave inside, which was nice for heating up food. There are Lawson and Seven-Eleven nearby, and it's very close to Hisaya-dori Station, making transportation quite convenient. However, the downside is that there is no free luggage storage service, and you have to use a paid locker, which costs 1,200 yen, and that felt quite expensive. I thought it would be good to keep this in mind.

name: Sanco Inn Grande Nagoya
detail: I used this hotel for a 2-night, 3-day stay for a conference. The reception staff were friendly, and their service was very polite. The lobby and room were clean, and it was especially convenient that the sink, toilet, and shower were separated by doors. I could see the night view from my room, and I was able to choose my favorite pillow at the pillow bar on the first floor, which allowed me to rest comfortably. There were plenty of outlets, which was convenient as well. I did find the refrigerator to be a bit small, and there was only one elevator going to the eighth-floor lobby, which could result in some waiting times depending on the time of day. The station, convenience stores, and bustling areas were also nearby, and at about 15,000 yen for 2 nights and 3 days, I think the cost performance was quite good. I would like to use this hotel again when I go to Nagoya.

name: Meitetsu Grand Hotel
detail: It is connected to Nagoya Station, so you can go there without getting wet even when it rains. The room's interior is somewhat dated, but it is clean. For breakfast, you can enjoy Nagoya specialties such as hitsumabushi, tebasaki, doteyaki, and kishimen. The freshly made omelet is also delicious! In the lobby, there is a welcome coffee service as well.

name: APA Hotel Nagoya Ekimae
detail: The accommodation is well-located, within easy walking distance to the core shopping district and convenient for shopping. The room is tidy and clean, with complete facilities. The building is situated in a quiet alley at night, ensuring good sleep quality. The staff are friendly and professional, with attentive service. Overall, it offers great value for money and is a recommended option.

name: Hostel Wasabi Nagoya Ekimae
detail: I checked in to a capsule hotel for the first time, feeling nervous, and there were separate spaces divided into two levels from A to H on each floor. I was in E-2, but it was surprisingly spacious and didn't feel cramped at all. Each shower room had a changing area, and the washroom was clean and very nice. Above all, it was close to the station and felt safe.

name: BASE LAYER HOTEL NAGOYA NISHIKI
detail: There was a 24-hour parking lot nearby for 1200 yen (with repeated visits). The hotel was also clean and convenient with keyless entry. Checking in and out was easy with QR codes. The coin laundry was 800 yen for washing and drying, which I found affordable and was happy about. The room was small, but it was only for sleeping, so it was not a problem. I didn't use the cups and other items as they were covered in dust. I opted to have breakfast at the coffee shop No. 7 right in front instead of at the hotel.
